title: What is Programming? An Overview
summary: Programming is the process of giving instructions to a computer to solve problems. This lesson introduces the basic idea of programming, its purpose, and how it differs from simply using software.

sections.heading: Definition of Programming
sections.body:
Programming is writing a set of commands that a computer can understand and execute. These commands are written in a programming language, which translates human ideas into machine actions.

When you program, you break a problem into smaller steps and tell the computer exactly how to perform each step.

sections.heading: Why We Need Programming
sections.body:
Computers can only do what they are told. Programming lets us create new tools, automate repetitive tasks, and solve complex problems that would be impossible to do by hand.

For example, a weather app uses programs to collect data, calculate forecasts, and display the results on your phone.

sections.heading: From Idea to Program
sections.body:
The typical flow starts with an idea, then you design an algorithm, write code in a language, test it, and finally run it on a computer. Each step refines the solution and catches mistakes early.

Think of it like cooking: you plan the recipe (algorithm), gather ingredients (variables), follow the steps (code), taste and adjust (debug), and serve the dish (run the program).

quiz.q: What is the main purpose of programming?
quiz.why: Programming is about writing instructions that a computer can follow.

quiz.q: Which term describes a step‑by‑step solution to a problem?
quiz.why: An algorithm is a precise sequence of steps to solve a problem.

quiz.q: Which activity is part of the programming process?
quiz.why: Debugging involves locating and fixing errors in code.

flashcards.back: A language used to write instructions for a computer.
A clear, ordered set of steps to solve a problem.
The actual text written in a programming language.
Finding and fixing mistakes in a program.
Software that helps you write, test, and run code.
